notes: Mobile App Transcript Design Pass; IOS-DESIGN.md says where the phone's unfolded Duo shots still differ from the desktop: the failure card's actions fill the card and lack Continue on another model, the fleet's sections carry counts, the proof rig's repeated pairings repeat titles, and one offset jump per transcript run remains at turn 6.; A fold keeps a scrolled-up reader on their row. On iOS 27.1 the transcript's List never reports scrollPosition(id:) and its cells get no geometry while UIKit scrolls them, so the rows' onAppear and onDisappear keep the keys on screen and the earliest in list order is the top row (TranscriptReflow.topRow), never moved while a reflow is open and read nothing per frame; the scrollPosition binding that never answered is gone. The Duo fold run's scrolled-up leg passes: the same top row at all four stops, the reflow anchored on it.; A fold-run stop that fails its check ends the unfold's recorder too, so no simctl recording outlives the proof.; The layout probe keeps its 500 events again (re-serialising 5,000 on every write is main-thread work a scroll proof should not carry); the Duo fold run's scripts/lib/duo_fold_sampler.py samples revealedUnits and draftChars and merges the app's event log every 400 ms instead, so the run keeps every event it wrote. scripts/ios-duo-checks.test.ts covers the merge.; The transcript's top row is back on scrollPosition(id:): a row's own onGeometryChange, against .scrollView or a space the list names, never fired while UIKit scrolled the cells, so it found no top row either. IOS-DESIGN.md says what is open: on iOS 27.1 the List never reports the top row, a fold leaves a scrolled-up reader where UIKit puts them, and the Duo fold run's scrolled-up leg fails on it.; A fold keeps the person's sidebar toggle: the split writes its visibility as it collapses and expands, and only a write in a split whose pose has held for half a second (ShellPose.keepsVisibilityWrite) is kept, so a sidebar hidden before a fold is hidden after it; the Duo proof's fold run caught the sidebar coming back. Half open, pose_check reads the thread's column from the sidebar's edge past the fold's band (48 pt at most) to the window less its safe area; the docs' pose table says portrait is always the pager (669 is under 680) and half open is two panes on the band.; The Duo proof shoots the thread matrix and checks every shot against the pose rules: in unfolded, unfolded-portrait and half-open, one seeded thread per type with the sidebar shown and hidden (TC_TEST_SIDEBAR), light and dark, the keyboard up and at accessibility-large, each shot's pose-<sessionId>.json copied beside its layout report. pose_check (scripts/lib/duo_pose_check.py) holds the sidebar's state as asked and its width to 260-320 pt (iOS 27.1 keeps it at 320; half open it follows the fold), the thread's column to what the sidebar leaves of the window less its safe area, the mode and columns to ThreadPose for that column (a board beside the sidebar is the pager, two panes once it is hidden), the measure to 768 or the column less 32, and the composer's box to the column's edges. The fold cycle is real: a streaming implementation thread with a draft and an undecided approval, run at the bottom and 700 pt up, checked by scripts/lib/duo_fold_check.py for the route, the draft (the composer's draftChars), one hSize, window and sidebar change per step, revealedUnits never going back, the reader's end or top row kept, and no row made twice. A transcript row now says when it straddles the top edge, since a List never reports scrollPosition(id:), so a fold anchors a scrolled-up reader on their row. The layout probe keeps 5,000 events; the shell notes sidebar, split.width and every write of the split's visibility; the thread screen notes body.frame. scripts/ios-duo-checks.test.ts tests both checks.
